title: Nosocomial Outbreaks
paragraphs: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) affect approximately 1 in 10 patients worldwide, causing significant morbidity, mortality, and economic strain on healthcare systems. Nosocomial outbreaks driven by person-to-person transmitted pathogens generate the most acute clinical and operational crises: triggering staff shortages, ward closures, and delayed procedures. Current control measures rely on broad testing and isolation protocols, but effective intervention requires identifying the specific drivers of an outbreak: such as patient zero, superspreaders, transmission routes, and undetected or imported cases.

NosoTrack is an outbreak analytics platform that infers who-infected-whom in real-time, enabling control teams to identify how infections spread and design targeted interventions before outbreaks escalate.

platform.title: How It Works
platform.subtitle: NosoTrack integrates various data streams into a unified Bayesian analytics engine that infers transmission chains in near real-time.

cards.desc: Pathogen genomes provide phylogenetic signal for transmission inference.
Bluetooth-enabled sensors record contacts between patients and staff.
EHR provide information on admission & discharge dates, ward assignments, and test results.

anonymisation.desc: Patient identifiers are stripped, hashed, and encrypted before analysis.

engine.desc: NosoTrack uses Bayesian inference to probabilistically reconstruct transmission trees (who infected whom).

features.title: Importation Events
features.desc: Identifies cases imported outside the hospital.

features.title: Transmission Patterns
features.desc: Characterises transmission patterns between wards, staff and patients.

features.title: Forecasting
features.desc: Projects short-term transmission risk for staff and patients.

alertsReports.desc: Control teams receive notifications when wards or individuals have an increased risk of infection, and when new transmission events or clusters are identified.

ipcSupport.desc: Infection Prevention and Control experts interact with an AI assistant to interpret outbreak dynamics and design intervention strategies. These strategies are evaluated by a simulation engine that projects potential outcomes, with iterative feedback to refine and identify the optimal intervention.

title: Methods & Software
research.intro: NosoTrack builds on over a decade of research in outbreak reconstruction, focusing on the integration of epidemiological, genomic and contact data to infer transmission trees. Our team and collaborators have published extensively on methodological advances, including the outbreaker2 R package and the linktree method for inferring transmission patterns between staff and patients. These methods have been applied to real outbreak data, including SARS-CoV-2 nosocomial outbreaks in Switzerland and the UK, MRSA in neonatal intensive care units in the UK, Klebsiella pneumoniae in a Nepali neonatal unit, Acinetobacter baumannii in hospitals in North Carolina, and Ebola outbreaks in the DRC. We are committed to open science, with all software freely available and publications accessible to the public.
research.timelineLabel: Evolution of Outbreak Reconstruction: Methods & Applications

timeline.description: Integrates genetic and epidemiological data using an SEIR model for transmission; assumes complete bottleneck and all cases observed/sampled; inference via maximum likelihood.
Reconstructs transmission trees from genetic data using a graph approach; minimizes total genetic distance; no explicit transmission model.
Bayesian method using mutations; SEIR transmission model with spatial kernel; single introduction.

Frames infectious disease transmission as a forensic problem; uses likelihood-based approach to identify who infected whom from epidemiological data; models serial interval and infectious period distributions.
Bayesian reconstruction combining epidemiologic and genomic data; SI transmission model; handles multiple introductions and sampled cases.
Simultaneous inference in BEAST framework; coalescent process; SEIR model with spatial kernel.
Uses likelihood ratio test for time of most recent common ancestor; Poisson mutation model; no explicit transmission model.
Bayesian method in R package; coalescent process; SI model; handles ongoing outbreaks and proportion of sampled cases.
Simultaneous inference in R package; coalescent process; SI model; all cases observed but not always sampled.

A modular platform for outbreak reconstruction; extends outbreaker with a flexible, module-based architecture allowing custom likelihood functions, movement models, and prior distributions; implemented as an R package.

Investigates when pathogen genome sequences are informative of transmission events; quantifies the relationship between genomic diversity, mutation rates, and the ability to resolve transmission links; provides guidance on when genomic data adds value to epidemiological investigation.

Bayesian inference of transmission chains combining timing of symptoms, pathogen genomes, and contact data; extends outbreaker2 framework to integrate contact tracing data as an additional source of information for transmission tree reconstruction.
Labels internal nodes in phylogenetic tree; weak bottleneck; no explicit transmission model.
Reconstructs phylogenetic tree from transmission tree; Jukes-Cantor model; all cases observed and sampled.

Bayesian framework combining genomic and epidemiological data using outbreaker2 to reconstruct transmission trees in a nosocomial SARS-CoV-2 outbreak; assesses limits of genomics for outbreak reconstruction.

timeline.method: Within-hospital transmission across two pandemic waves
timeline.description: Combines viral genomic and epidemiological data from 2,181 participants across two pandemic waves at a UK NHS Trust using Bayesian transmission reconstruction; reveals a shift from staff-to-staff to patient-to-patient transmissions between waves, and finds that hospital-onset cases drove most onward transmission.
Combined retrospective epidemiological and genomic study using outbreaker2 to reconstruct transmission chains of SARS-CoV-2 amidst multiple outbreaks in a geriatric acute-care hospital.

Uses a Bayesian framework to infer transmission pairs by exploring all compatible transmission trees based on symptom dates, incorporating a wide range of incubation period and generation time distributions; derives serial intervals from reconstructed pairs, stratified by variants, to account for negative serial intervals.

A framework to estimate group transmission assortativity from transmission chain data, quantifying the extent of within-group vs. between-group transmissions while accounting for group sizes and depletion of susceptibles; implemented in an R package.

A statistical framework implemented in the R package mixtree to compare epidemic forests (collections of plausible transmission trees) using chi-square test and PERMANOVA for detecting differences in transmission dynamics.

founder.name: Dr Cyril Geismar
founder.bio: Postdoctoral research fellow. PhD in mathematical modelling of infectious diseases at Imperial College London, focused on SARS-CoV-2 outbreak reconstruction. Executive board member and developer for the R Epidemics Consortium. Teaches outbreak analytics at Emory University and LSHTM.

advisors.name: Dr Anne Cori
advisors.bio: Associate Professor specialising in real-time outbreak analysis and epidemiological parameters. Lead author of EpiEstim and co-author of outbreaker. Develops statistical methods for outbreak reconstruction and rapid transmissibility assessment.

advisors.name: Dr Thibaut Jombart
advisors.bio: Associate Professor specialising in outbreak response analytics, biostatistics, population genetics, and R programming. Lead author of outbreaker and founder of the R Epidemics Consortium. Field experience in Ebola deployments in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

advisors.name: Dr Shaun Truelove
advisors.bio: Associate Professor focused on infectious disease dynamics and modelling for public health response and policy (COVID-19, influenza, vaccine-preventable diseases). Co-leads the US Scenario Modeling Hubs and ACCIDDA, a consortium producing epidemic scenario projections and forecasts.

title: Next Steps
roadmap.intro: We are seeking funding to validate and deploy NosoTrack in two stages.

phases.title: Simulation Study
phases.desc:
Conduct simulation studies under realistic operational constraints to determine the conditions under which NosoTrack improves outbreak control.
This phase will assess NosoTrack's effectiveness across pathogens, hospital settings, and levels of data availability.

phases.title: Pilot Study
phases.desc:
Deploy the platform in a 1–2 year pilot, integrating EHR and Bluetooth-enabled contact tracing in a live hospital environment.
This phase will generate real-world evidence on reduced infections, cost savings, and improved hospital capacity management.
